subject: Private hosting intake — environment activation checklist & handoff
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@cloudbridge.com>; eng@cloudbridge.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private hosting intake — environment activation checklist & handoff

Hi Asha / CloudBridge team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for the private-hosting footprint. Attached is a concise activation checklist tailored for your VPC + on-prem connector setup (file: 20261108-environment-activation-checklist.xlsx). The goal here is to get to a Day-0 smoke run within your target 2-week window.

Quick summary of required items (high level):
- Account & billing: CloudBridge tenant ID + PO or SOW (we have the PO on file; confirm billing contact)
- Networking: egress IP allowlist, ingress load-balancer endpoints, internal DNS names to be reserved
- Identity & secrets: service account with roles, KMS/HSM key identifier (optional for customers with HSM)
- Access: bastion/jumpbox policy and list of engineer IAM emails
- Telemetry: metrics/trace endpoints and log forwarding details

Questions we have for you before we kick the provisioning pipeline:
1) Will you provide a pre-provisioned peering connection or prefer Redwood to initiate the peering and hand off the Cloud-side config?
2) Do you require HSM-backed encryption for model artifacts or is KMS sufficient?
3) Any egress restrictions to specific subnets (we received a CSV draft but need confirmation)?

Action owners I suggest: Redwood infra (Kimberly) owns peering and KMS guidance, Marissa will coordinate Ops runbook and smoke test, Ben will coordinate scheduling and PAP (pre-activation plan) with your engineering lead.

Next step: Asha, can you share the final egress IP list and confirm if CloudBridge will manage the peering or want Redwood to initiate? If you prefer a call, propose 30 minutes tomorrow in the morning PT.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: 20261108-environment-activation-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), network-egress-ip-list.csv (CSV stub)

From: Asha Reddy <asha@cloudbridge.com>

Cc: eng@cloudbridge.com
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 12:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private hosting intake — environment activation checklist & handoff

Ben — thanks for the checklist and the clear owners. A few quick answers: 

- Peering: we'd prefer Redwood to initiate the peering and provide the Terraform snippet for our infra team to apply. We want to keep control of the Cloud-side apply.
- KMS/HSM: for now KMS is sufficient; we may request HSM for the production tier later.
- Egress: attaching an updated CSV (see network-egress-ip-list.csv). Note that our security team also requires that all egress traffic is restricted to a set of /28 ranges; those are included.

Two items from our side:
1) Can you confirm the expected port list for the runtime control plane and for outbound model telemetry? We need that for the firewall ACL.
2) For the bastion access, we need a short-lived certificate flow (we use the internal CA), do you support cert-based SSH or just key-based?

We can do a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00 PT. Please send an invite.

—Asha
Asha Reddy
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudBridge

Thanks Asha — quick answers from infra/security perspective: 

- Port/egress list: control plane uses TLS outbound on 443 for telemetry and heartbeats; runtime nodes require 10250 (kubelet) for our admin agent when you expose the internal management plane; model runtime egress for artifacts uses 443. We will provide a definitive table in the Drive link (see related_links). If you are on a closed firewall we can deliver an HTTP proxy option — but that adds ~50ms latency for artifact pulls.

- SSH auth: Redwood supports SSH key-based access for bastion by default. We can integrate certificate-based short-lived access via your internal CA using an SSH proxy jump configuration; that path requires a one-time config on the bastion (we manage the proxy) plus a small cert-rotation hook on your side. If you want us to own the proxy cert rotation we can include that as part of the Dedicated runbook.

Notes on KMS vs HSM: KMS is fine for pre-prod. For HSM we need an offline key ceremony plan and HSM vendor details — that'll extend timeline by ~2–3 weeks.

I've attached the initial port matrix and a short-runbook excerpt as comments in the Drive file. Marissa / Ben, I'm happy to own the peering Terraform snippet — will push as a gist and share before the call.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: port_matrix.md (Drive), peering-snippet.tf (Gist pending)
